concepts.name: Weil positivity criterion
concepts.plain: A quadratic form built from primes, the archimedean place and the pole. RH holds exactly when it is never negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1952: RH ⇔ W(f∗f̃*) ≥ 0 for all test f; equivalently the Hermitian form 𝒬 is positive, ⇔ a unitary Hilbert realization of the scaling flow (TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1 (iv)).
pitfalls: The zero-side check is tautological (TAA Lemma 142); only the prime side with no zeros is a test.
"Q = LP + positive" is false (TAA Lemma 8).

rels.note: TAA Lemma 142: Weil form = relative intersection matrix on translates
Spec ℤ analogue of Hodge index on V₀ (TAA Lemma 91)

concepts.name: Davenport–Heilbronn function
concepts.plain: Has a functional equation but no Euler product, and zeros off the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: DH is a location test only (no Euler product, TAA Lemma 103). Tail 0.7398 (TAA Lemma 78) vs 0.7376 (TAA Lemma 136).
pitfalls: Tail number conflict.

concepts.name: ψ(x) − x (explicit formula, deviation from the pole)
concepts.plain: Count prime powers with weight log p and subtract the pole’s prediction x; what remains is a sum over zeros. RH ⇔ the remainder is O(√x log²x).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Explicit formula ψ(x) = x − Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ − log 2π − ½log(1 − x⁻²); RH ⇔ ψ(x) − x = O(x^{½+ε}). In TAA the x term is the pole/𝕃 reference; ψ − x ≠ 0 measures the flow-relative H¹.
concepts.uncertain: The explicit-formula wording is standard (cited), not from a specific lemma section.
pitfalls: ψ(x) − x ≠ 0 is not a failure: it is the zero contribution relative to the pole reference.

rels.note: both compare a prime product/sum to a pole reference

concepts.name: Primitive part V₀ = U^⊥
concepts.plain: What is left after removing the reference plane; on it the form should be negative (curves: theorem; ℚ: RH).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D° = D − d₁f₂ − d₂f₁; (D°)² = −Tr_{H¹}(α_Dα_D†) (TAA Lemma 133). Over ℚ V₀ = U^⊥ and D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91).
pitfalls: A “−2Tr” formula holds only on the primitive part.

concepts.name: Lagarias/Hinkkanen criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the log-derivative of ξ has positive real part to the right of the line.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Lagarias 1999 (1.5), credited to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemmas 17, 146).

concepts.name: Missing: arithmetic Castelnuovo object (positive involution on a space where the Weil distribution is a |·|²)
concepts.plain: A space with an infinite H¹, a positive involution † and a flow u_t with u_t u_t† = eᵗ, on which the explicit-formula (Weil) distribution becomes a squared norm, with that positivity proved without using the zeros.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object = (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = eᵗ, (C4) positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136); equivalently a positive involution plus a Frobenius-type flow with positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136 synthesis). Hilbert–Pólya form: a positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); “all that is missing is an appropriate inner product” (Lax–Phillips, TAA Lemma 105/TAA Lemma 141).
concepts.proved: Over F_q: Ax2 ∧ Ax3 ⇔ |α| = √q (TAA Lemma 137, theorem). Over ℚ: isometry of the flow is unconditional (TAA Lemma 1); the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign (TAA Lemma 138); Ax2 alone holds for fakes, Ax3 alone is tautological (TAA Lemma 137).
concepts.tests: Must separate ghosts: Ax2 and Ax3 jointly, never one alone (TAA Lemma 137). Must not define the inner product by Weil’s form (circular, TAA Lemma 138 R2; TAA Lemma 106).

concepts.name: Missing: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch for Spec ℤ (D8)
concepts.plain: The top substantive direction: a surface S over Spec ℤ with an ample class and a Riemann–Roch whose χ(nD) is quadratic, so that Hodge index follows as it does for curves.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: D8: surface + ample + RR for Spec ℤ — find S with χ(nD) quadratic and a Hodge index; obstacle: the collapse ℤ ⊗ ℤ = ℤ; sign = Weil form (TAA Lemma 140, TAA Lemma 141). Acceptance test (TAA Lemma 141): reconstruct the relative space and its form from independent constraints — (a) the hyperbolic plane U = ⟨𝟙, 𝕃⟩, (b) the scaling flow acting on it as diag(1, eᵗ), (c) ampleness at ∞, (d) RR/GRR with quadratic growth — then prove negativity on U^⊥. Any proof that uses the zeros, or defines the form by its negativity, fails.
concepts.proved: Over F_q: surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (Segre 1937, Grothendieck 1958) (TAA Lemma 140). Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65). Arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K) satisfy V1–V3, but the relative part is Néron–Tate, not ζ (TAA Lemma 145).
concepts.tests: Must pass the tautology test (no zeros, no definition by negativity, TAA Lemma 141) and the must-fail-for-DH test (TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: flow-relative H¹ for Spec ℤ
concepts.plain: For ℚ both cohomologies we can compute vanish (étale H¹ = 0, Arakelov Pic⁰ = a point), yet ψ(x) − x ≠ 0. The zeros need a cohomology relative to the scaling flow.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 H¹ table: Spec ℤ has étale H¹ = 0, Arakelov Pic⁰ = point (r = 0, h = 1), relative count ψ(x) − x = −Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ + …, infinitely many zeros, flow H¹ = Deninger H¹_flow (Open). “For ℚ both H¹’s that we can compute vanish, yet ψ − x ≠ 0, so the zeros need a cohomology relative to the flow” (TAA Lemma 141, restatement).
concepts.formula: N_n − (1 + qⁿ) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) ↔ ψ(x) − x = −Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ + …
concepts.proved: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1 ⇒ H¹ét = 0 (TAA Lemma 140); curve row: N_n − (qⁿ + 1) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) with relative Gram NSD (TAA Lemma 141 §1); Tr ↔ −(ψ − x) up to the s = 0 term and ARCH (TAA Lemma 142 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must carry a positive structure (Ax2), not only the trace formula: the explicit formula alone is ghost-blind in data (TAA Lemma 143: ghost defect ≤ 1.9e−5, 0.08× noise).

concepts.name: Missing: quadratic Riemann–Roch + “ampleness ⇒ effectivity” on the square
concepts.plain: A Riemann–Roch on Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ whose Euler characteristic is quadratic in D, together with the step “ample ⇒ has sections ⇒ effective”. This is exactly the part of the curve proof that Spec ℤ lacks.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Classical chain: S1 quadratic RR, S2 Serre duality, S3 h¹ ≥ 0 / Minkowski, S4 sections ⇒ effective, S5 ample·effective > 0. Missing Spec ℤ step = quadratic S1 + S4 (“ampleness ⇒ effectivity” via a 2-dim h⁰) (TAA Lemma 145 V3, verdict VF-E). Parity: quadratic χ is even in D, linear χ odd ⇒ fixed rank proves only degree c(D) = 0, never sees D².
concepts.uncertain: The displayed “needed shape” is the classical surface RR, quoted as the target form.
concepts.proved: Every proved Connes–Consani RR is 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const (TAA Lemma 147); fixed-rank products are linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400 (TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear); on ℙ¹_ℤ χ̂ is quadratic and realizes the U-form (TAA Lemma 145). Hodge index also needs S2, S3, S5 (TAA Lemma 145 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must fail for Davenport–Heilbronn, hence must use the Euler product (TAA Lemma 147, necessary condition). Must see D², i.e. be quadratic. V3 on the square ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH, so it must be proved, not assumed (TAA Lemma 145).

concepts.name: Missing: an inequality consequence of automorphy (SC-E / HS-1)
concepts.plain: Automorphy (invariance under the full modular group) decides where the zeros are but does not derive it; what is missing is an inequality that automorphy forces on δ_ρ.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: SC-E (structural P: Hecke/Euler product) = Selberg-class RH, the open non-circular version of trapped-set rigidity (TAA Lemma 143); sharpened to “an inequality consequence of automorphy” (→ Weil positivity, TAA Lemma 142) (TAA Lemma 144). HS-1: an automorphy-defect functional 𝒟(Λ_X) ≥ 0 with 𝒟 = 0 ⇔ Λ_X = ξ; it needs an inequality that the defect forces on δ_ρ, which we do not have (TAA Lemma 144).
concepts.proved: Thm 3.3 (TAA Lemma 144): automorphy picks a = 1/ξ(2s), c = φ uniquely, exact defect formula; Hecke alone puts no constraint on φ (Prop 3.2). SC-A ⇔ RH (restatement); SC-B false (DH); SC-C false (all cofinite Γ); HS-B (Hecke + unitarity ⇒ δ = 0) false (fakes).
concepts.tests: Fakes pass Hecke/FE/Δ/unitarity to 1e−25 but fail S-invariance: DH by 1.4–3.2%, the degree-0 ghost by 4.5e−6–1.6e−4 (TAA Lemma 144). The inequality must be violated by both.

concepts.name: Missing: a BRST-type complex Q with H(Q) = U^⊥ positive (PM-3)
concepts.plain: A nilpotent operator on the test functions whose cohomology is exactly the relative space U^⊥, so that “remove the pole plane, then the rest is positive” becomes a cohomology statement, as in Gupta–Bleuler/BRST.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: PM-3: Gupta–Bleuler/BRST complex Q on TAA Lemma 142’s test functions with H(Q) = U^⊥ (TAA Lemma 146). Thm gb (linear algebra, proved): for V = U ⊕ U^⊥, U = ⟨F₁, F₂⟩, F_i² = 0, F₁F₂ = 1, the quotient F₁^⊥/⟨F₁⟩ is isometric to U^⊥; a nilpotent Q with cohomology U^⊥ would package it as a flow-relative cohomology (Open).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ; “no ghosts” ⇔ RH (restatement); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya). TAA Lemma 146: the BRST quartet decouples, but a ghost quartet survives.
concepts.tests: A ghost quartet is exactly a quartet that fails to decouple (TAA Lemma 146); the complex must not decouple it. Positivity of the quotient is an input in QED and is RH for ζ.

concepts.name: Missing: H¹ on the square of the scaling site (Connes–Consani s(f,f) ≤ 0)
concepts.plain: A first cohomology on the square of Connes–Consani’s scaling site; with it, an RR theorem would give D(f)•D(f) ≤ 0, which is RH.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: CC18: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0, s(f,f) = D•D with D = ∫fΨ_λ; five steps, only step 1 (complex lift) built; H¹ on the square of the scaling site, and hence RR there, is open (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). ½D(f)•D(f) = ½s(f,f) is the Weil form (TAA Lemma 142).
concepts.proved: No RR for C_ℚ × C_ℚ exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). The square exists as a site with Ψ_λ (TAA Lemma 30) but carries no H¹, RR or Hodge index (TAA Lemma 65).
concepts.tests: All H⁰-side objects built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70) (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: a Néron–Severi strictly larger than U containing the Frobenius classes Ψ_λ
concepts.plain: An intersection theory on the square in which the Connes–Consani correspondences Ψ_λ are genuine classes outside the pole plane U, with enough sections that their growth sees s(f,f).
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Need NS ⊋ U with Ψ_λ, and #H⁰(±nD(f)) ≥ 2^{n² s(f,f)/2} (TAA Lemma 147). Decisive missing objects: H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR (TAA Lemma 147 (iv)).
concepts.proved: Laurent piece of HZ ∧_𝕊 HZ: box count 2n² + 4n exact, but the quadratic coefficient 2αβ is the U-form ⇒ vacuous on degree-0 D(f) (TAA Lemma 147 Thm vac).
concepts.tests: Quadratic growth must come from V₀ = U^⊥, not from U (Thm vac). Ghost-sensitive side is s(f,f), which must be negative for ζ and fail for DH (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: passivity of ξ′/ξ from a zero-free mechanism (Lagarias margin)
concepts.plain: RH is equivalent to ξ′/ξ being a passive (positive-real) response to the right of the line. What is missing is a proof of a passivity margin that uses only primes, the pole and the archimedean place.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Lagarias (1.5), attributed to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemma 146, opened). PM-1: a Lagarias margin h(σ) for ξ vs DH/ghost — a provable, ghost-sensitive passivity margin? (TAA Lemma 146).
concepts.formula: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 for Re s > ½
concepts.proved: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²): each zero an absorption line, an off-line zero a gain line (TAA Lemma 146). Passivity ⇒ causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146 corrections). Free positivity (Λ(n) ≥ 0, KMS, Bagchi recurrence) is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 136, TAA Lemma 118).
concepts.tests: Grid σ ∈ [.505, 1.1], t ∈ [80, 92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; ghost −66.97, 1.94% (TAA Lemma 146). The margin must stay positive for ξ and go negative for both.

concepts.name: Missing: RR/GRR on an arithmetic Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ producing the sign (RG-5, “the missing row”)
concepts.plain: In the relative Gram dictionary every entry has an analogue except the one that proves the sign: a Riemann–Roch or Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem on an arithmetic square.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: RG-5: RR/GRR on an arithmetic “Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ” producing the sign — the missing row of the TAA Lemma 142 dictionary (TAA Lemma 142). D9: arithmetic GRR test on the scaling-site square (TAA Lemma 140/TAA Lemma 141 candidate).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 142 Thm 1.1: Weil Gram on translates is Toeplitz (flow), POLE = rank-2 signature (1,1) = the curve U-part exactly; every entry zero-free (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); G_rel ≤ 0 on all spans ⇔ RH (Weil, restatement). Unconditional sign only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch-only a* (TAA Lemma 127), both ghost-blind.
concepts.tests: Ghost ⇒ n₊(G_rel) = 2 (TAA Lemma 142); DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45. The theorem must produce G_rel ≤ 0 for ζ on every span without using zeros.

concepts.name: Passivity (positive real part)
concepts.plain: A system that never produces energy; its impedance has non-negative real part. For ξ′/ξ this is Lagarias’ criterion.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Passivity ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s > ½ ⇔ RH (Lagarias/Hinkkanen). Passivity ⇒ causality (TAA Lemma 146, correction 3).
concepts.formula: Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 for Re s > ½
pitfalls: Not independent of causality.

concepts.name: Relative Gram matrix G_rel
concepts.plain: Take a test function, translate it, and form the matrix of pairings after removing the pole plane. RH ⇔ this matrix is positive (semi)definite for all choices.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: G_rel(f; t_i) with zero-free entries (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); G_rel ⪰ 0 ∀ ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH. Unconditional only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch a* (TAA Lemma 127).
pitfalls: Using the zero side to "check" it is tautological.

concepts.name: Riemann–Roch strategy: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0
concepts.plain: Connes–Consani’s plan: build divisors D(f) on the square from test functions; RH is equivalent to their self-intersection being ≤ 0, and an RR theorem there would prove it.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: CC18: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0 (12), s(f,f) = D•D with D = ∫fΨ_λ (14); five steps, only step 1 (complex lift) built; H¹ on the square open. ½D(f)•D(f) = ½s(f,f) is the Weil form (TAA Lemma 147 §4, TAA Lemma 142).
pitfalls: The H⁰ side is ghost-blind; only the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (TAA Lemma 147 §4).

concepts.name: Light cone U = ⟨𝟙, 𝕃⟩ (pole plane, null rays)
concepts.plain: The two special directions (the trivial class 𝟙 and the Lefschetz/pole class 𝕃) span a plane with one positive and one negative direction; positivity is always measured relative to it.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Over F_q: U = ⟨f₁, f₂⟩ ⊂ NS(C×C), signature (1,1), f₁, f₂ null; ample class lies in U; complement negative definite. Over ℚ: the pole/Tate plane spanned by 𝟙 and 𝕃 (poles at s = 0, 1), U^⊥ = V₀ (TAA Lemma 142).
pitfalls: "Light cone" includes its interior.
The ample class lives in U; the surface is read relative to the points.

concepts.name: Ax1–Ax3 axioms (Yoneda specification)
concepts.plain: The three ingredients that together force RH for curves: Hodge index on Frobenius graphs (Ax1), a positive involution † (Ax2), and ππ† = q for that same † (Ax3).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 137: on T_W, |α| = √q ⇔ Ax2 ∧ Ax3 ⇔ Ax1 ∀N. Each axiom alone is ghost-blind (Ax3 alone tautological; Ax2 alone holds for fakes); only the joint requirement separates. All qualifying items are over F_q; no Spec ℤ item qualifies.
numbers: 7 of 135 items in the programme’s positivity inventory pass (TAA Lemma 137)
pitfalls: Ax3 (unitarity, ππ† = q) is satisfied by ghosts too; never present it as positivity.

concepts.name: Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8)
concepts.plain: The curve proof needs a surface, an ample class and Riemann–Roch.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D8 (TAA Lemma 140): surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index. TAA Lemma 145 V3: classical S1 quadratic RR, S2 Serre, S3 h¹ ≥ 0, S4 sections ⇒ effective, S5 ample·eff > 0; the missing Spec ℤ step is quadratic S1 + S4. TAA Lemma 147: CC18 calls exactly this "the key missing step".
pitfalls: Needs S2, S3, S5 too (TAA Lemma 145).

concepts.name: Tensor square HZ ∧_𝕊 HZ and its Laurent piece (quadratic only in U)
concepts.plain: The tensor square of ℤ over the sphere spectrum is bigger than ℤ and has a Laurent-polynomial piece; its sections grow quadratically, but the quadratic term is only the U-form, so it is vacuous on the degree-0 divisors that matter for RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC16 Prop 7.4: HZ ∧ HZ ≇ HZ, assembly onto ℤ[t^±]^{⊗k}/ℤ. TAA Lemma 147 Laurent model (t-degree ≤ nβ, coefficient ≤ 2^{nα}): box count 2n² + 4n exact; ℓ² ball counts = volume to 4.8e−6 (n = 10), log₂ # = 2n² − n log₂ n + O(n); coefficient 2αβ is the U-form ⇒ vacuous on degree-0 D(f) (Thm vac). Needed: NS ⊋ U containing Ψ_λ with #H⁰(±nD(f)) ≥ 2^{n² s(f,f)/2}.
concepts.formula: log₂ # = 2n² − n log₂ n + O(n); quadratic coefficient 2αβ = U-form
pitfalls: Quadratic growth here comes only from U, so it says nothing about the primitive part V₀ (Thm vac).

concepts.name: Parity argument: linear χ cannot see D²
concepts.plain: A Riemann–Roch whose Euler characteristic is linear (odd) in D can prove "positive degree ⇒ sections" but never contains D²; a quadratic (even) χ is needed for Hodge index.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145: quadratic χ is even in D, linear χ odd ⇒ fixed rank only proves degree c(D) = 0, never sees D². TAA Lemma 147: for CC23, χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 for deg₂D ∉ ℤ (even part constant 2χ(𝒪), odd part ⌈deg₂D⌉′); χ(D) + χ(K−D) = 0 except −1 on deg₂ ∈ (−2,0) (observation).
pitfalls: χ-symmetry is an observation, not a CC claim (TAA Lemma 147 s2).

concepts.name: Tautology boundary (zero side vs prime side)
concepts.plain: Checking positivity using the zeros themselves is circular; a real test must use only primes, the pole and the archimedean place.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: all entries of the relative Gram are zero-free (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); sign = RH (Weil); the zero-side check is the tautology. Unconditional sign only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch-only a* (TAA Lemma 127), both ghost-blind.
pitfalls: "Without zero locations" is vacuous in finite models (Newton identities, TAA Lemma 109).

concepts.name: Deninger’s foliated program
concepts.plain: Deninger’s program: a foliated dynamical space whose leafwise cohomology carries the zeros; a positive Hodge star plus the flow would force Θ = ½ + (skew part).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 4: foliation-like (Deninger) structure carries the explicit formula with its signs; contact-like (Reeb) gives only the analytic shadow; on closed M, Reeb flows and Deninger systems are mutually exclusive. TAA Lemma 28: zeros = leafwise zero modes [analogy/conjectural]. TAA Lemma 50 Prop 7.1 (Den98): positive J commuting with Θ ⇒ Θ − ½ skew [RESTATEMENT]. TAA Lemma 93: Deninger D1–D5 stated exactly. TAA Lemma 141 §2: level S3 of the "surface" target.

concepts.name: No étale H¹ for Spec ℤ
concepts.plain: Spec ℤ is simply connected; the "H¹" must be relative to the flow (ψ − x ≠ 0).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 140: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1 ⇒ H¹ét = 0. TAA Lemma 141 §4: H¹ table with a flow-H¹ column; Q(√2) circle length √2·log(1+√2) = 1.24645 (Schoof). The H¹ that carries zeros is flow-relative (ψ − x).

concepts.name: Rosati positivity
concepts.plain: An involution † on endomorphisms with Tr(φφ†) > 0 — like a squared length that is never negative. With ππ† = q it forces |α| = √q.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Tr(φφ†) > 0 on End⁰(J); ππ† = q ⇒ |α| = √q (Milne AV 14.3). On R[F]: Rosati PD ⇔ RH-model ⇔ ∃ compatible J with [J,F] = 0; n₋ = #real pairs + 2#quartets (TAA Lemma 106). Over ℚ: Rosati = Weil form is a restatement.
pitfalls: |φ| = 1 on Re s = ½ is only the adjoint half ππ† = q (Ax3), ghost-blind.
Positivity over F_q is geometric, from intersection numbers, not arithmetic (TAA Lemma 106, correction 1).

rels.note: Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant (TAA Lemma 99)

concepts.name: Castelnuovo–Severi inequality
concepts.plain: On the surface C×C a class cannot be "too timelike" relative to the two fibre directions; applied to Frobenius graphs it gives RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D² ≤ 2(D·f₁)(D·f₂); def(D) = 2d₁d₂ − D² = −(D°)² = Tr_{H¹}(α_D α_D†) (C–S = Rosati, TAA Lemma 133). Weil mF + n: −(2gqm² + 2amn + 2gn²) ≤ 0 ⇔ a² ≤ 4g²q (TAA Lemma 125).
numbers: primitive Gram det 4p − a² > 0 (29 primes, L133)
pitfalls: A “−2Tr” formula holds only on the primitive part with the g-dimensional trace.

concepts.name: Arithmetic unitarity ("RH = unitarity")
concepts.plain: TAA’s founding claim made precise: the scaling flow is always an isometry of the Weil form; RH is the statement that this form is positive, so the flow is genuinely unitary.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1: (ii) T_t is a 𝒬-isometry unconditionally; (iii) growth exponent = Θ − ½; (iv) RH ⇔ 𝒬 ≥ 0 ⇔ unitary Hilbert realization ⇔ bounded matrix coefficients.
pitfalls: Isometry is free (Ax3-like); positivity of the form is the content (Ax2).

concepts.name: RH for curves over F_q (Weil)
concepts.plain: For a curve over a finite field the Frobenius eigenvalues all have size √q. This is the one setting where TAA’s positivity is a theorem.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1948: Castelnuovo–Severi / Hodge index on C×C ⇒ |α_i| = √q. Proved without the zeros: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch ⇒ Hodge index ⇒ sign.
pitfalls: Weil already did column 2 (1940 note, 1948 books); the open step is column 3.

concepts.name: Ghost quartet ½ ± δ ± iγ
concepts.plain: A fake set of four zeros off the line, replacing a pair ½ ± iγ, used to test whether a criterion can detect RH failure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103 convention: replace ½ ± iγ by ½ ± δ ± iγ; each quartet gives 2 negative Weil eigenvalues; onsets L* listed.
pitfalls: δ convention conflict: δ = β − ½ (TAA Lemma 25/TAA Lemma 103/TAA Lemma 143) vs δ_ρ = 2β − 1 (TAA Lemma 144).

concepts.name: Goldfeld’s theorem (Euler product at s = 1 ⇒ RH, analytic order)
concepts.plain: If the partial Euler product of L(E,s) at the centre behaves like C/(log x)^r, then L(E,s) satisfies RH and r is the analytic order of vanishing — with a surprising √2 in the constant.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: If ∏_{p≤x} L_p(E,1) ∼ C/(log x)^r then L(E,s) satisfies RH, r = ord_{s=1}L(E,s), C = L^{(r)}(E,1)/(r! √2 e^{rγ}) (Goldfeld 1982, cited via Conrad 2005; TAA Lemma 140).
pitfalls: It gives the analytic order, not the rank (rank = order is BSD).
a_p are not BSD generators.
Note the √2 factor (Conrad).

rels.note: prime data vs the reference at s = 1

concepts.name: Decay rate ¼
concepts.plain: Every scattering resonance of the modular surface decays at rate ¼ exactly when its ζ-zero is on the line; an off-line zero decays at (1−β)/2 instead.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally, poles at ρ/2 symmetric about ¼, rate (1−β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates ¼ [R]. TAA Lemma 120: spectral rate ¼, not uniform. TAA Lemma 143 SC-A (L + unitarity ⇒ κ ≡ ¼) ⇔ RH; ringing rate 0.24996 vs predicted ¼. TAA Lemma 144: μ = ¼ for every ρ (FE), ghost and DH ring at 0.0957414 = (1−β)/2.
concepts.formula: rate = (1 − β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates = ¼
pitfalls: The circular line for the modular surface is Re s = ¼, not ½ (TAA Lemma 143 corrections); rate = (1−β)/2, not Re ρ/2 (TAA Lemma 143 corrections).
No essential spectral gap for the modular surface (Bourgain–Dyatlov 1612.09040).

concepts.name: Fake Weil polynomials (finite ghosts)
concepts.plain: Polynomials that look like curve zeta numerators (functional equation, integer counts) but have roots off the circle. They are the F_q test ghosts.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Fakes pass FE, count positivity, mod-2 data and the Hecke lattice (1,2); they fail Hodge index on ⟨H,V,Δ,Γ_{Fⁿ}⟩ (n₊ ≥ 2) and Rosati. Mixed fake (T² − 6T + 7)(T² + 7) passes N ≤ 2, fails from N = 4 (TAA Lemma 137, TAA Lemma 141).
pitfalls: Degenerate fakes (|α| ∈ {1, q}) cause pole-degenerate exceptions (TAA Lemma 92 C9).

concepts.name: Compatible complex structure J commuting with Frobenius
concepts.plain: A quarter-turn that commutes with Frobenius and makes the form positive; it exists exactly when the curve satisfies RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: J = (2F − a)/√(4q − a²) (TAA Lemma 101) exists only if a² < 4q; 2^g sign choices, exactly one positive. Finite: compatible J with [J,F] = 0 ⇔ F unitary semisimple (TAA Lemma 104). For ζ: J exists ⇔ RH (restatement, TAA Lemma 104 dichotomy).
numbers: g = 1, q = 101: J = J_F exact; ghosts give Cl(1,1)
pitfalls: A quartet J is symplectic but never compatible (sig (2,2)) (TAA Lemma 110).
With a W-independent form J is unconditional but ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 104).

concepts.name: Connes trace formula
concepts.plain: Connes’ trace formula on the adele class space: zeros appear as an absorption spectrum, and the global trace formula holding is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Connes 1999 (read at source, TAA Lemma 30/TAA Lemma 71): global trace formula ≡ RH; Thm 1 sees only critical zeros (δ > 1); Thm 5 char p; zeros = absorption spectrum (TAA Lemma 71). TAA Lemma 82: cutoff, non-critical zeros as resonances. TAA Lemma 118: Connes reduces RH for Hecke L to the trace formula ⇒ Weil positivity; absorption spectrum ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 138 R2: Hilbert–Pólya positivity is circular if the inner product is Weil’s form.

concepts.name: de Branges spaces
concepts.plain: Hilbert spaces of entire functions built from a Hermite–Biehler function E; RH becomes "E_h is Hermite–Biehler", but de Branges’ stronger positivity conditions are known to fail for ζ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36 Thm 3.1: for h ∈ (0,½], all β ≤ ½ + h ⇔ PR on σ > ½ + h ⇔ E_{h′} HB ∀h′ > h; h = ½ free, h → 0 = RH. Conrey–Li 2000 (opened, TAA Lemma 78): de Branges positivity fails for ζ and χ₄. TAA Lemma 118: Ψ_c passive ⇔ E_c = ξ(·+c) Hermite–Biehler. TAA Lemma 34: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side.
pitfalls: Conrey–Li: de Branges’ stronger conditions fail — beware "positivity ⇒ RH" shortcuts.

concepts.name: Epstein zeta no-go
concepts.plain: Epstein zeta functions of binary quadratic forms have a functional equation but no Euler product, and they have zeros off the line — the classic counterexample class next to DH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 83: Epstein x² + 5y² = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅); N(200) = 253 zeros, 183 on the line (70 off-line); first off-line 0.93297 + 15.66825i. TAA Lemma 135: 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250; control x² + y² (= 4ζL(χ₋₄), has Euler product): 0. TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion and FE hold, unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm).

rels.note: TAA Lemma 135 counts vs quadratic positivity

concepts.name: Hasse bound as a positive degree form
aliases: Q_p = x² + a_p xy + p y²
concepts.plain: For an elliptic curve the degree of an endomorphism is a positive quadratic form; Hasse’s bound is that this form is positive (Cauchy–Schwarz / Pythagoras).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: deg(m + nπ) = m² + amn + qn² is PD ⇔ a² < 4q; Hasse = Cauchy–Schwarz. Ghost a = 25, q = 101: deg(10 − π) = −49 (TAA Lemma 106).
concepts.formula: m² + a mn + q n² > 0 ⇔ a² < 4q

concepts.name: Li criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the Li coefficients are non-negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Li 1997 / Bombieri–Lagarias 1999: RH ⇔ λ_n ≥ 0 for all n — the Weil positivity in another basis. TAA Lemma 112 reads the Weil form as a Toeplitz–Carathéodory problem; TAA Lemma 131: no route supplies the positivity.

concepts.name: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side
concepts.plain: A de Branges / transmission-line object built from prime data whose passivity along the whole line is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Su21 (Suzuki JFA 281 (2021) 109116): E^{ω,ν} = ξ(½ + ω − iz)^ν, νω > 1, Hankel kernel from prime-side data (TAA Lemma 34). TAA Lemma 37: headline exponential line Θ_c = exp(−2c ξ′/ξ); ‖𝒦[t]‖ < 1 ∀t ⇔ sup ≤ 1; weak form sup_t ≤ 1 ⇔ RH; "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; strict pointwise bound open (M11).
pitfalls: "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; the correct form is sup ≤ 1 (TAA Lemma 37).

concepts.name: Bagchi recurrence
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ ζ approximates itself in the strip (strong recurrence).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Bagchi (via Nakamura Thm B): RH ⇔ strong recurrence of ζ for all K, ε ("infinite prime bath still recurs", TAA Lemma 118). TAA Lemma 123 local form [T given Voronin + Carlson]: ζ strongly recurrent on a disc K ⇔ no zero on K; ghosts show up as a local Rouché defect. Finite prime baths recur but are ghost-blind.

concepts.name: de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ
concepts.plain: Heat flow on ξ; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao), RH ⇔ Λ = 0.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable (TAA Lemma 111). Healing times TAA Lemma 124/TAA Lemma 136 conflict.
pitfalls: t* = 2δ² vs δ²/2.

concepts.name: Frobenius as a boost (rapidity ½ log q)
concepts.plain: On the light-cone plane Frobenius acts like a Lorentz boost of rapidity ½ log q; a true curve needs one boost, a fake needs two.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hodge index + one boost of rapidity ½ log q on the H–V plane ⇒ Hasse; fakes need two (TAA Lemma 98 thm:fqboost). Over ℚ: translation is an isometry, pole boost rapidity ½ log λ; Lorentzian = Weil positivity (restatement).
concepts.formula: B_{½ log q}(H + V) = Γ/√q (hyperbolic part)
pitfalls: Dividing by √q does not undo the boost (TAA Lemma 114, correction 14).
Two boosts are never a pure rotation unless inverse (TAA Lemma 107).

rels.note: Levinson/Szegő step = boost of rapidity artanh|α| (TAA Lemma 98, TAA Lemma 117)

concepts.name: Gain lines (active media)
concepts.plain: A ghost acts like a gain line: negative absorption.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §2: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²) — each zero is an absorption line to its right; an off-line zero gives a gain line. Grid σ ∈ [.505,1.1], t ∈ [80,92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; TAA Lemma 144 ghost −66.97 (1.94%). Lorentz model: dRe χ/dω −6 (absorber) / +6 (gain).

concepts.name: Integer dimension over 𝕊 (minimal generators)
concepts.plain: On Spec ℤ̄ Connes–Consani’s dimension is an integer: the least number of generators over the sphere spectrum. The log-theta dimension of van der Geer–Schoof is a different, "virtual" count that agrees up to a bounded error.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [N]: brute force dim_𝕊(HZ)_[−m,m] = n + 1 for all m ≤ 16; dim_𝕊[±1] = ⌈log₃(2n+1)⌉ for all n ≤ 40; dim_𝕊 − vdGS h⁰/log 2 ∈ [1.016, 1.983]. TAA Lemma 147, correction 1: Dim_ℝ on C_p is a covering dimension, not a theta count.
pitfalls: Do not identify CC dimension with theta/lattice counts (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Hodge index theorem
concepts.plain: On a surface the intersection form has exactly one positive direction (the ample class); everything orthogonal to it is negative. This sign is what proves RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: NS(C×C) ⊗ ℝ has signature (1, ρ−1); U = ⟨f₁,f₂⟩ is the (1,1) part and its complement is negative definite. Over ℚ, Hodge-index form on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91, restatement). Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8).
concepts.formula: sig NS = (1, ρ − 1); D·D ≤ 0 on h^⊥
pitfalls: Effectivity and Hodge index are independent on both sides (TAA Lemma 94).
Hodge index needs S2, S3, S5 too (TAA Lemma 145).

rels.note: D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ over ℚ (TAA Lemma 91)
U^⊥ = physical quotient (TAA Lemma 115, TAA Lemma 146)

concepts.name: Lax–Phillips scattering
concepts.plain: Scattering theory for waves on the modular surface; resonances relate to zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: LP80 (read at source, TAA Lemma 118/TAA Lemma 141): s(z) = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s), Res_{s=1} = 3/π, poles at zeros of ζ(1+2iz), RH ⇒ Im z = ¼; Pavlov–Faddeev "RH iff Z″ decays exponentially"; spectrum of B″ = {(κ−1)/2}; "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product". TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally.
pitfalls: LP (6.19) rate sign ambiguous in OCR (TAA Lemma 118, correction 7).

concepts.name: Cartan involution / compact unitary group
concepts.plain: A positive involution is the same thing as a compact (rotation-type) symmetry group; Albert lists the possible kinds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Positive involution ⇔ compact unitary group (TAA Lemma 99, Milne Prop 1.20); Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant of J; Weil numbers generate CM or totally real fields (TAA Lemma 136); Albert types I–IV.
pitfalls: Abelian scaling has only an outer Cartan U(1); zeros-as-angles = RH (circular, TAA Lemma 99).

rels.note: no compact Hodge circle for ℚ (TAA Lemma 100)

concepts.name: Connes–Consani sites
concepts.plain: Topos-theoretic candidate for Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Arithmetic site and scaling site (CC14, CC16): a square exists, with Ψ_λ and s(f,f) = D•D (TAA Lemma 30), but no H¹, RR or Hodge index on it (TAA Lemma 65). TAA Lemma 147: their proved RRs are 1-dimensional; RR on the square is open (CC18).

concepts.name: Pole plane / Tate poles at s = 0, 1
concepts.plain: The two poles of ξ(s) at s = 0 and 1 give the reference plane; subtracting them is what makes a form "relative".
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: the relative Gram on translates uses the pole terms f̂(0), f̂(1) (zero-free entries). Pole of ζ at s = 1 is the 𝕃-ray; the functional equation pairs it with s = 0.

concepts.name: Products grow linearly (2n), not quadratically
concepts.plain: Sections on naive products of Spec ℤ̄ grow only linearly in n (slope 2); a genuine surface needs quadratic growth, which forces the rank to grow with n.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [T/N]: product sandwich ⌈log₂ #⌉ ≤ dim_𝕊(box) ≤ Σ dims, exact = additive bound in 6/6 boxes; fixed rank ⇒ linear: Spec ℤ̄² fits 1.99993n + 2.0009 (vs 2n + 4); quadratic growth ⇒ rank ≳ n. Same as TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear (fixed-rank lattice ⇒ h⁰ linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400).

concepts.name: Yoneda specification
concepts.plain: Specify the object by its properties (Ax1–Ax3).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 90: bare Hom sets do not determine an object (ℚ vs ℚ^(N)); naturality needed; representability ⇒ uniqueness/functoriality, presupposes positivity if it is an axiom. TAA Lemma 98 Prop 6.1: representable ⇒ unique; 𝔉(pt) ≠ ∅ ⇒ RH; "representability is the whole battle" (TAA Lemma 98, correction 19). TAA Lemma 137: T_W with Ax1–Ax3; existence open.

concepts.name: Organizing split: ghost-blind = phase, ghost-sensitive = sign
concepts.plain: Every test that ghosts pass is about phase/unitarity; every test that catches a ghost is about the sign of a spectral weight, and for ζ that sign is RH.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 synthesis: functional equation, |φ| = 1, cocycles, Hecke, cusp positivity are ghost-blind (Ax3); Lagarias sign, Weil sign, Rosati sign are ghost-sensitive (Ax2) and ⇔ RH for ζ. Every ghost-sensitive global quadratic statement for Spec ℤ found so far is a restatement.
numbers: DH: FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8
pitfalls: An organizing observation, not a theorem: "sign" items for curves are theorems, for ζ restatements.

concepts.name: Must-fail-for-DH acceptance test
concepts.plain: Any future Riemann–Roch on the square must be false for Davenport–Heilbronn; otherwise it cannot prove RH. So it has to use the Euler product.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: All H⁰-side objects are built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ and are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (TAA Lemma 142: DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70). Hence an RR theorem on the square must FAIL for DH ⇒ must use the Euler product / ring structure (necessary condition, proposed acceptance test, TAA Lemma 147).
pitfalls: A necessary condition only.

rels.note: proved RRs pass DH, so cannot decide RH

concepts.name: BRST / Gupta–Bleuler physical quotient
concepts.plain: Remove null and negative-norm states to get a positive physical space — as U^⊥ in Hodge index.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ [T]; "no ghosts" ⇔ RH [R]; missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya) ⇒ restatement. TAA Lemma 146 §3: Gupta–Bleuler F₁^⊥/F₁ ≅ U^⊥; the BRST quartet decouples but the ghost quartet survives. PM-3 (BRST complex with H(Q) = U^⊥) open.
pitfalls: PM-3 is open.

concepts.name: Two-point form g + iω ≥ 0
concepts.plain: Combine a metric g and symplectic ω into one Hermitian form; positivity ⇔ Weil.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103: g + iω ≥ 0 ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH.

concepts.name: Riemann hypothesis (target node)
concepts.plain: All nontrivial zeros of ζ have real part ½. In TAA every ghost-sensitive global sign statement for Spec ℤ turns out to be RH restated.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: RH is not proved in TAA. The positivity inventory of the programme finds that every ghost-sensitive global quadratic statement for Spec ℤ is a restatement of RH.
concepts.formula: ρ = β + iγ, β = ½ for all ρ
pitfalls: Every lemma PDF carries "RH NOT proved".

concepts.name: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object (C1–C4)
concepts.plain: Requirements an arithmetic surface would need to reproduce the curve proof.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 136: an arithmetic Castelnuovo object needs (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = e^t, (C4) positivity proved without zeros; circularity flagged (TAA Lemma 106). TAA Lemma 138: the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign. TAA Lemma 147: the decisive missing objects are H¹ on the square, an NS ⊋ U containing Ψ_λ, and quadratic RR.

concepts.name: No Riemann–Roch for C_ℚ × C_ℚ (the square is open)
concepts.plain: There is no Riemann–Roch theorem for the square of the scaling site; Connes–Consani themselves list H¹ on the square, and hence RR there, as open.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147, correction 2: "their RR for the square / C_ℚ × C_ℚ, if it exists" — it does not exist; CC18 states H¹ on the square of the scaling site, and hence RR there, is open. TAA Lemma 147 (iv): decisive missing objects = H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR.
pitfalls: Do not cite a CC Riemann–Roch on the square: none exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2).

concepts.name: Hilbert–Pólya
concepts.plain: Find a self-adjoint operator with spectrum the γ’s.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Standard program: a self-adjoint/unitary realization with spectrum the γ’s would give RH. TAA verdicts: spinor route = Hilbert–Pólya in Clifford dress (TAA Lemma 104); 2B″ + ½ needs an inner product (TAA Lemma 105, LP80 "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product"); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); circular if the inner product is Weil’s form (TAA Lemma 138 R2); lossless Heaviside realization = Hilbert–Pólya [O] (TAA Lemma 144 HS-F).

concepts.name: Ghost onset L* ≈ log(γ/2π)
concepts.plain: The smallest window at which a ghost quartet can be detected; it grows like the log of the ghost’s height.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103: onsets L* = 0.90, 1.15, 1.70, 3.45 for the test ghosts; L* ≈ log(γ/2π).

concepts.name: Källén–Lehmann spectral positivity
concepts.plain: Physical theories have non-negative spectral weight; ζ analogue is the sign of zero weights.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §3: Källén–Lehmann / R(s) positivity is an Ax2 statement (spectral weight ≥ 0; CMT05, WP20 6931(40)e−11). TAA Lemma 146 corrections: KL positivity needs a positive metric — exactly what is missing for ζ.
pitfalls: KL needs a positive metric (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).

concepts.name: Time delay (Wigner)
concepts.plain: How long a wave packet lingers in the cusp; unlike the winding of the phase, the time-delay peak does see ghosts.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 143: winding ½ per zero for all β (ghost-blind), but time-delay peak at r = 42.85 is 3.09 (ζ), 27.22 (ζ + TAA Lemma 103 ghost), 27.42 (DH): ghost-sensitive. ζ time delay is negative for r ≲ 2.9 (min −3.87), so "positive delay" fails for ζ. TAA Lemma 120: dwell time ∂_x log|Φ| = −θ′(ω). TAA Lemma 118: Connes harmonic measure of an off-line zero = (1/2π) × TAA Lemma 117 excess group delay.
pitfalls: Positive time delay fails for ζ (TAA Lemma 143 corrections).

concepts.name: Chebyshev bias for elliptic curves (averaged sign of a_p)
concepts.plain: Individual signs of a_p are phase data, but their running average is biased, and the bias is governed by the zeros of L(E, s) and the analytic rank, in the same way ψ(x) − x is governed by the zeros of ζ. An off-line zero would make the averaged sign blow up like a power of x.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Proposed comparison (TAA Lemma 150 plan): averaged sign of a_p for 11a, 37a, 389a and 32a (y² = x³ − x) against ψ − x; ties to Goldfeld’s product ∏ L_p(E,1) ∼ C/(log x)^r. Under RH the bias is a log-scale effect; an off-line zero gives power-law growth. The literature citation for an elliptic-curve Chebyshev bias is to verify and is not given.
concepts.uncertain: to verify: the Chebyshev-bias citation for elliptic curves is unverified (not opened); no reference given.
pitfalls: Literature citation to verify: none is given until opened at source.

rels.note: averaged error term governed by zeros

concepts.name: Displaced reference (subtracting the pole)
concepts.plain: Arithmetic quantities are measured relative to a reference fixed by the pole; the "error" is the displacement from that reference.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: ψ − x, E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) and the relative Gram all subtract a pole/reference term. TAA Lemma 146 records this as an organizing analogy.
pitfalls: Analogy, not theorem.

rels.note: buoyancy: weight relative to displaced fluid

concepts.name: Negative index κ(𝒬) = N₊ (ghost count)
concepts.plain: Counts how many negative directions the Weil form has; each off-line zero quartet contributes exactly 2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Unconditional: κ(𝒬) = N₊ (TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1); each ghost quartet gives 2 negative eigenvalues (TAA Lemma 103, Bombieri). Finite form: n₋ = k_r + 2k_c = ½ rk E² (TAA Lemma 110 Thm 2.3); Rosati n₋ = k = τ + ½Z_off = n₊(NS) − 1 (TAA Lemma 88 Thm B).
pitfalls: Count convention: TAA Lemma 91 n₊ = 2k vs TAA Lemma 88 k = ½Z_off — see TAA Lemma 92 C5 notation clash.

rels.note: Rosati index on R[F] = Weil index (TAA Lemma 106)

concepts.name: Krein collisions (how ghosts are born)
concepts.plain: Zeros on the line carry a sign; two can only leave the line together if they meet with opposite signs.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 111: semisimple unit-spectrum F strongly stable ⇔ Krein form definite on each eigenspace; ghosts born only at opposite-sign collisions (710/710 births). For ζ the graphical Krein sign alternates ⇒ no protection; Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable.
pitfalls: Krein = stability, not positivity; presupposes unit spectrum (TAA Lemma 111 circularity).

concepts.name: Two partners of a zero (duality vs conjugation)
concepts.plain: Every zero has a duality partner (from the functional equation) and a conjugate partner; RH says the two coincide.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 93 Thm 1.1: duality partner (Poincaré duality/cup product, ghosts too) and conjugation partner; RH ⇔ partners coincide. Rosati Tr(p(F)p(F)†) and the Weil zero side have the same "zero × duality partner" shape.

rels.note: mirror ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄ fixes ρ ⇔ β = ½

concepts.name: Ghost conventions (δ, heat-flow healing)
concepts.plain: Bookkeeping for ghost parameters across lemmas; several conventions disagree.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: δ = β − ½ (TAA Lemmas 25, 103, 143) vs δ_ρ = 2β − 1 (TAA Lemma 144). Heat-flow healing time t* = 2δ² (TAA Lemma 124) vs δ²/2 (TAA Lemma 136).
pitfalls: Always state which δ is used.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch on Spec ℤ̄ (1-dimensional)
concepts.plain: Connes and Consani proved Riemann–Roch for the compactified Spec ℤ, counting sections by integer numbers of generators; it is a one-dimensional "χ = degree + constant" law and cannot see D².
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: CC23 Thm 1.1/5.1 over 𝕊: dim H⁰ − dim H¹ = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (genus 0, base 2, no exceptional set); CC22 over 𝕊[±1]: ⌈(deg D + log 2)/log 3⌉′ − 1_L, duality H⁰(K−D) ≅ Hom(H¹(D), U(1)_{1/4}), K = −2{2}; scaling site Thm 5.17 Dim_ℝ H⁰(D) − Dim_ℝ H⁰(−D) = deg D. Verdict (TAA Lemma 147): all proved RRs are 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const ⇒ blind to D² by TAA Lemma 145 parity.
pitfalls: RR is for the Arakelov compactification Spec ℤ̄, not Spec ℤ; two versions, the 𝕊 one supersedes 𝕊[±1] (TAA Lemma 147, correction 3).
Dim_ℝ is a Lebesgue covering dimension on C_p, not a theta count (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Automorphy defect (TAA Lemma 144)
concepts.plain: How far a function fails to be modular, packaged as a cocycle; it is phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 144: defect is a cocycle; ghost-blind. "Cocycles give structure, not sign."

concepts.name: Certified positivity windows
concepts.plain: Computer-certified intervals on which the Weil form is positive.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Certified windows: progress log reaches e² and hybrid e^2.4; one text says "stop at 1.6". All below ghost onsets, ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 142).
concepts.uncertain: Which extent is current needs a check of the progress log.
pitfalls: Source conflict: "stop at 1.6" vs progress log to e², e^2.4.

concepts.name: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations
concepts.plain: Pairing a holomorphic form with its own complex conjugate gives a positive number: a genuine |amplitude|².
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: HR holds on every compact Riemann surface; HR form = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Positivity = complex structure inserted (Weil operator C = i^{p−q}). Hecke self-adjointness gives a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
pitfalls: Column 2 (F_q) never fully inherited the HR sign; Castelnuovo replaces it algebraically (TAA Lemma 140).

rels.note: cup with the conjugate through the Hodge structure

concepts.name: Weil operator C = i^{p−q} = Wick rotation
concepts.plain: Turning an indefinite pairing into a positive one by inserting a quarter turn — the same move as Wick rotation in physics.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 139: Q indefinite → Q(C·, ·̄) PD (Rosati); Abel–Jacobi = principalization. A complex structure is a μ₄ action (J² = −1). Obstruction: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has no complex structure.
numbers: y² = x³ − x: π/√p primitive 4th root of unity for p ≡ 3 mod 4 (L140)
pitfalls: The Fourier transform is the swap, not the Weil operator (TAA Lemma 140).
Over F_q the sign is algebraic (Castelnuovo); the Hodge model is only an analogy there (TAA Lemma 139 caveat).

rels.note: no complex structure on Pic^ ≅ ℝ

concepts.name: √2 family
concepts.plain: Geodesic from 1 + √2; it is not singled out.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §1: traces t_k = 6, 34, 198, 1154, 6726 (Pell), lengths kℓ₀, ℓ₀ = 4 log(1+√2) = 3.5255; length-ordered series is periodic (period 2πi/ℓ₀ = 1.7822i) ⇒ cannot carry ζ zeros; conductor-ordered = h⁺R(8)ζ(s−1)/L(s,χ₈). TAA Lemma 146, correction 2: √2 is not the first norm −1 unit (φ is smaller).
pitfalls: √2 is not the first norm −1 unit; the golden ratio is smaller (TAA Lemma 146).

concepts.name: Pole of ζ at s = 1 (residue / 3/π)
concepts.plain: ζ has a pole at s = 1; the Eisenstein series E(z,s) has its pole there with residue 3/π, the reciprocal of the area of the modular surface.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Res_{s=1} E(z,s) = 3/π = 1/vol(SL₂(ℤ)∖ℍ); E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) is the non-holomorphic correction (TAA Lemma 144/TAA Lemma 145 context).
pitfalls: The point 1 is not ∞.

concepts.name: Toeplitz / Verblunsky coefficients
concepts.plain: Positivity of Toeplitz matrices ⇔ |α_n| < 1; each step a boost of rapidity artanh|α|.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 112 [C Simon]: Carathéodory–Toeplitz–Herglotz; T_{n+1} ≻ 0 ⇔ |α_j| < 1 ∀j < n; n₋(T_N) = #{E_n < 0}, sign flips at each |α_j| > 1. Levinson: PD ⇔ |κ_j| < 1, each step a boost of rapidity artanh κ (true |κ| < 1 for 60 orders; ghost κ₈ = −1.0009). TAA Lemma 117: U(1,1) boost of velocity |α|; |α| > 1 = Krein swap ∘ boost. TAA Lemma 37/TAA Lemma 118: Schur/Verblunsky layer stripping = restatement (circular).

concepts.name: Closed geodesics on the modular surface
concepts.plain: Lengths 2 log ε_t from traces t; Selberg trace formula pairs them with resonances.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Length 2 log ε_t with h⁺ classes (TAA Lemma 143); trace-6 has 3 primitive oriented classes (TAA Lemma 141); counts t = 3..11: 1,2,2,3,3,4,2,6,3. √2 geodesic ℓ = 3.5254943481, sinh(ℓ/2) = 2√2; golden geodesic 1.9248 is shortest. S(t) = Σ h⁺ log ε⁺², 36 discriminants 0 mismatches (TAA Lemma 143).

concepts.name: S-mirror ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄
concepts.plain: Reflecting across the critical line; a zero is fixed exactly when it is on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ fixed by ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄ ⇔ β = ½.

concepts.name: Selberg resonances
concepts.plain: Poles of φ(s) relate to ζ zeros at s = ρ/2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s) has poles in Re s < ½ exactly at ρ/2, φ(½) = −1 (TAA Lemma 143). ΣΛ(P)N^{−s} = Z′/Z(s) − Z′/Z(s+1). TAA Lemma 143: ρ/2 seen in the length spectrum from class numbers (projection on the predicted ζ term 1.003). Selberg zeros ρ/2: infinitely many off the line (TAA Lemma 141).

concepts.name: Arakelov geometry
concepts.plain: Compactified arithmetic surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 74: Ô(1)² = ½ for FS metrics; pole-plane Gram [[½,1],[1,0]] signature (1,1); Hodge index vacuous in genus 0. TAA Lemma 139: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has rank 1 and no complex structure. TAA Lemma 65/TAA Lemma 145: Faltings–Hriljac = Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K), relative part = Néron–Tate, not ζ. TAA Lemma 138 R5: Néron–Tate PD (37a1 ĥ = 0.051114).

concepts.name: Cusp ≠ archimedean place
concepts.plain: The cusp of the modular curve and the archimedean place of ℚ are different objects, though both get written ∞.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The cusp is a point of the modular curve; the archimedean place is a valuation of ℚ. Neither is the frame bundle, and ∞-toposes are unrelated to the infinite place.
pitfalls: Do not identify cusp, place ∞, frame bundle, ∞-topos.

concepts.name: Density / volume reading
concepts.plain: The modular surface’s volume form and the half-density: area π/3 gives degree 1/12, and the half-density y^½ is the Heaviside ½ — structure, not sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §7: c₁(ω, Pet) = dxdy/(4πy²); area π/3 ⇒ deg ω = 1/12 = −ζ(−1); χ_orb = −1/6; half-density y^½ unitary L²(dr) → L²(dy/y²) = Heaviside ½. TAA Lemma 145: the U-form is indefinite, not a volume (TAA Lemma 145 corrections); volume formula for h⁰ is heuristic.
pitfalls: Volume form ≠ Levi-Civita connection (TAA Lemma 141 list).

concepts.name: F₁ base
concepts.plain: The hoped-for "field with one element" under Spec ℤ. Over F₁ the single Frobenius trace becomes a sum over all zeros, and Connes–Consani take the sphere spectrum 𝕊 as F₁.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 65: a_p is the right model, but over F₁ the single trace becomes Σ_ρ u^ρ (one eigenvalue per zero, infinite genus, N(1) = −∞); for curves the CC dictionary is literal (u = qⁿ, α_i = q^{ρ_i}). CC10 N(u) positive on (1,∞) is prime-side and shared by Beurling systems ⇒ cannot force RH alone. TAA Lemma 147, correction 4: "On the metaphysics of F₁" proves no new RR; it restates CC23 and discusses 𝕊 as F₁.
pitfalls: CC N(u) is only formal (TAA Lemma 65 C1).

concepts.name: Principalization
concepts.plain: Making divisors principal; Abel–Jacobi = principalization (TAA Lemma 139).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 60: "principalization as hamiltonization"; clutching = principalization (analogy). TAA Lemma 71: curve version theorem — #Pic⁰(F_{pⁿ}) = |1 − πⁿ|²; on Spec ℤ only the ℝ>0 boost (blind to θ_p). TAA Lemma 73: class group = obstruction to integral spinor square roots of light rays. TAA Lemma 139: Abel–Jacobi = principalization.

concepts.name: Spec ℤ is terminal
concepts.plain: Spec ℤ has no base to fiber over, unlike a curve over F_q.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65 THM), so the "square" must be built elsewhere (arithmetic site, Borger). TAA Lemma 137: Spec ℤ is terminal ⇒ Yoneda gives uniqueness only. TAA Lemma 140: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1.

concepts.name: Spinor/Clifford route
concepts.plain: Encode J and F as a Clifford pair; ghosts give the indefinite Cl(1,1).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 101/TAA Lemma 110: ghosts give Cl(1,1); true case Cl(2,0).

concepts.name: Weil Rosetta stone
concepts.plain: Weil’s analogy number fields / function fields / Riemann surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 140: Rosetta table (loop, H¹, 1 ⊕ 𝕃, counts, involution, sign); the Spec ℤ sign cell is missing (Weil positivity ⇔ RH). Column 2’s sign is the dim-2 algebraic shadow of Hodge–Riemann (surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index). Weil’s 1940 letter quotes read at source (Krieger, Notices 52(3)).

concepts.name: Cohesion (arena)
concepts.plain: Cohesion is the arena, not the surface.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §3: cohesion is the arena, not the surface; the étale ∞-topos of Spec ℤ is not cohesive (pro-shape, Hoyois); new Thm: [ℕ^×, Set] is not cohesive (Γ has no right adjoint). D10 (relative cohesion). TAA Lemma 146 §5: the cohesion quadruple Π ⊣ Disc ⊣ Γ ⊣ coDisc is a line without sign; RLGC is a 2×2 grid with mirror/KK/sign — numerology only.
pitfalls: Heaviside ≠ cohesion one-to-one.

concepts.name: Local-to-global failure
concepts.plain: Local positivity at each prime does not imply global.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25 Rem 6.2: naive local positivity fails (K < 0 for |r| < 6.28984); CC21 Thm 1 local archimedean positivity only for supp ⊂ [2^{−½}, 2^{½}] with vanishing. TAA Lemma 64/TAA Lemma 65: local Hasse (Q_p > 0 at every p, proved) vs global RH for L(E,s) (open) — the collective split. TAA Lemma 66: local positivity via Deligne weights is ghost-blind residual data.

concepts.name: Kramers–Kronig relations
concepts.plain: Causal response: real (dispersive) and imaginary (absorptive) parts determine each other. Absorption’s sign is the passivity condition.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146: dispersion = phase (ghost-blind), absorption sign = passivity ⇔ Lagarias ⇔ RH.
pitfalls: Passivity implies causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146).

concepts.name: Gribov ambiguity
concepts.plain: In QCD the gluon propagator violates positivity (it changes sign in Euclidean time) — the physics example of a "spectral weight" that is not positive.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §3: Gribov C(t) re-derived to 1e−16, first sign change t* = π/(2√2 M) = 1.1107 (in units of M). Interpretation as positivity violation is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).
pitfalls: Gluon positivity violation as confinement evidence is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).

concepts.name: Functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s)
concepts.plain: ζ’s completed version is symmetric under s ↦ 1 − s. Ghosts satisfy it too, so it cannot prove RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s); DH satisfies FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8 off the line (TAA Lemma 146). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Symmetry is phase data, never sign.

concepts.name: Gauss-sum unitarity |g| = √p (RH for a CM curve as a unitarity identity)
concepts.plain: A quadratic Gauss sum has absolute value exactly √p: this is the statement that the finite Fourier transform is unitary. For the CM curve y² = x³ − x and p ≡ 1 mod 4, the Frobenius eigenvalue is a Gaussian integer π with ππ̄ = p, so RH for this curve is the same kind of unitarity identity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |g|² = p (checked numerically for all odd p ≤ 691) = Plancherel for the finite Fourier transform, the same |x|^{½} twist as TAA Lemma 145. For p ≡ 1 mod 4, π ∈ ℤ[i], ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π, so |α| = √p is automatic. Over ℚ the analogue |ε| = 1 of a root number holds for Davenport–Heilbronn too: necessary, not sufficient. Open: a ζ-analogue in which the eigenvalue itself is a Gauss sum.
concepts.formula: |g|² = p, ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π
pitfalls: Unitarity identities of this kind are Ax3 (phase); over ℚ they are satisfied by DH too and cannot replace the sign.

rels.note: CM case: |π|² = p as a norm identity

concepts.name: E₂ anomaly (E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy))
concepts.plain: E₂ fails to be modular; fixing it costs a non-holomorphic term 3/(πy) tied to the pole. One reading treats the failure as a 2-class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E₂(−1/z) = z²E₂(z) + 12z/(2πi)… corrected by E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy), modular of weight 2. Ghost-blind (phase/automorphy data).
concepts.uncertain: Exact transformation constant quoted from standard theory; the 2-class reading is conjectural.

concepts.name: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (Connes–Consani RR)
concepts.plain: The χ in the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch is an Euler characteristic: sections minus obstructions of a divisor D. It is a number attached to D, not a character of a Galois group.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC23 over 𝕊: χ(D) = dim H⁰(D) − dim H¹(D) = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (TAA Lemma 147). TAA Lemma 145 parity: a linear χ is odd in D and never contains D²; the Hodge-index step needs a quadratic χ (D²/2 term). TAA Lemma 147: χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 (deg₂D ∉ ℤ).
pitfalls: Notation clash: this χ is an Euler characteristic, not the character χ (or ω) of the 691 class-group eigenspace.

concepts.name: Herbrand–Ribet: ω¹⁻ᵏ eigenspace of Cl(ℚ(μ_p)) and p | B_k
concepts.plain: The p-part of the class group of ℚ(μ_p) splits into pieces labelled by powers of the Teichmüller character ω. The piece ω¹⁻ᵏ is nonzero exactly when p divides the Bernoulli number B_k; for p = 691, k = 12 this is the ω⁻¹¹ piece.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For odd p and even k, 2 ≤ k ≤ p−3: A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) ≠ 0 ⇔ p | B_k (Herbrand 1932 ⇒, Ribet 1976 ⇐). p = 691, k = 12: B₁₂ = −691/2730, class in ω⁻¹¹ = ωᵖ⁻¹² (same character, since ω has order p − 1); odd character ⇒ minus part. TAA Lemma 66: 691 has two irregular indices (12, 200), so Cl/691 is 2-dim (ω⁻¹¹, ω⁻¹⁹⁹); ρ_{Δ,691} ss = 1 ⊕ ω¹¹, the non-split extension gives the ω⁻¹¹ class via CFT (Greenberg–Monsky lattices).
pitfalls: Notation: det ρ_Δ = χ_cyc¹¹ (cyclotomic character), whose reduction mod 691 is ω¹¹; the class itself sits in ω⁻¹¹ (TAA Lemma 66).
Ribet 1976 used weight-2 forms on Γ₁(p), not Δ.
Some authors write ωᵖ⁻¹²; it is the same eigenspace.

rels.note: size statement implied by the main conjecture
sizes, not signs: ghost-blind residual data (TAA Lemma 66)

concepts.name: Mazur–Wiles main conjecture ("Euler characteristic = L-value")
concepts.plain: The size of each Teichmüller piece of the class group (and of the Iwasawa module up the cyclotomic tower) equals the p-part of an L-value; slogan: an algebraic Euler characteristic equals an analytic L-value.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Mazur–Wiles 1984: characteristic ideal of the χ-part of the Iwasawa module = ideal of the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function. Finite-level consequence: #A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) = p-part of L(0, ωᵏ⁻¹) (Ribet, Berkeley slides). TAA Lemma 66: main conjecture = Hilbert–Pólya-type with free p-adic unitarity (γ eigenvalues are 1-units); μ = 0 is not a positivity; no positivity found on the Iwasawa side (OPEN).
pitfalls: Iwasawa theory measures sizes (orders, characteristic ideals), never the sign of D²; it cannot by itself give Weil positivity.
"Euler characteristic = L-value" is a slogan (Heuristic wording), the theorem is the equality of ideals.

concepts.name: Archimedean place and Γ_ℝ factor
concepts.plain: The "prime at infinity": its Gamma factor contributes a term to the Weil form that can be positive or negative depending on the window.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Γ_ℝ contributes the arch functional to W; arch-only positivity holds on thresholds a* (TAA Lemma 127), ghost-blind.
pitfalls: ∞ is not the frame bundle.

concepts.name: Cusp forms & Petersson positivity
concepts.plain: Cusp forms have positive Petersson norm — a real positivity, but it does not see ζ’s zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ⟨f,f⟩ = ∫|f|²y^k dμ > 0; HR = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind for ζ (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: Positive but about cusp forms, not ζ’s spectral weights.

concepts.name: Ramanujan congruence τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691 (Δ ≡ E₁₂)
concepts.plain: The cusp form Δ agrees with the Eisenstein series E₁₂ modulo 691, because 691 divides the numerator of ζ(−11). It is the meeting point of the Eisenstein (reference) and cusp-form (primitive) parts of the Hecke algebra.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691; ζ(−11) = −B₁₂/12 = 691/32760 (constant term of E₁₂ ∝ ζ(−11)/2 = 691/65520, TAA Lemma 70). TAA Lemma 66: τ(p) ≡ 1 + p¹¹ mod 691 for all 9592 p < 10⁵; Hecke congruence moduli N_k = |num(B_k/2k)| = 691, 3617, 43867, … (k = 12, 16, 18, …); bridge = closed point where Eisenstein and cuspidal components of Spec 𝕋 meet. TAA Lemma 70 (Mazur77 at source): Eisenstein ideal 𝕋/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/n, modulus = numerator of an Euler-depleted ζ(1−k); cusp encodes it as a negative zeta value; positivity invisible (timelike f ≡ spacelike E).
pitfalls: The congruence is mod 691 data: it says nothing about the sign of the Weil form (TAA Lemma 66: bridge = where positivity is lost).
E₁₂ has all its zeros off Re s = 6 (unconditional, TAA Lemma 66) — an "all ghost" Euler product.

rels.note: weight-12 rung: E₁₂ reference vs Δ primitive
Eisenstein = reference, cusp form = primitive split

concepts.name: Tate count / Picard number (ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Counting algebraic classes on C×C does not see whether eigenvalues are on the circle.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ(C×C) = 2 + Σ m(λ)m(q/λ) (Tate 1966, S–S §14.6); = 2g for squarefree, fakes too (TAA Lemma 93 Prop 2.3).

concepts.name: Hecke operators
concepts.plain: Averaging operators on modular forms; self-adjointness gives real eigenvalues but not the Ramanujan bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hecke self-adjoint ⇒ a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: a_p are not BSD generators.

concepts.name: Primary sign rule for a_p of y² = x³ − x
concepts.plain: For p ≡ 1 mod 4 write p = a² + b² with b even; the sign of a in a_p = 2a is fixed by a 2-adic normalisation (a + b ≡ 1 mod 4). The individual sign is phase data; RH is about the size |a_p| ≤ 2√p, not the sign.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: p = a² + b², b even, a_p = 2a with a + b ≡ 1 mod 4 (π primary mod (1 + i)³); checked for all 14 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 120 (p = 5, 13, 17: a_p = −2, 6, 2). The individual sign is a 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); RH = |a_p| ≤ 2√p is a size statement. The distribution of the signs (Sato–Tate for CM curves) is a separate question; no citation given here.
concepts.formula: a_p = 2a, p = a² + b², a + b ≡ 1 mod 4
concepts.uncertain: Sato–Tate/Hecke–Deuring citation for CM sign distribution not verified; none given.
pitfalls: The minus sign in a₅ = −2 is not the positivity sign of RH: it is a phase (choice of primary generator), and RH bounds the size.

rels.note: the sign of a_p is not the Castelnuovo sign

concepts.name: Archimedean thresholds a*
concepts.plain: Largest window size where the archimedean part alone is positive.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 127: a*_S2 < 0.5976773 (supersedes TAA Lemma 121’s 0.602); TAA Lemma 98 states a ≤ 1 in another normalization. Ghost-blind.
concepts.uncertain: Normalization between TAA Lemma 98 and TAA Lemma 127 not reconciled here.
pitfalls: Source conflict: TAA Lemma 98 "a ≤ 1" vs TAA Lemma 127 a* < 0.5976773 (different setups/normalizations to check).

concepts.name: Maass–Selberg relations
concepts.plain: Norm of truncated Eisenstein series expressed via φ and φ′; positivity there is automatic.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §8.1: Maass–Selberg ‖Λ^T E‖² minimum 0.611 (ζ) vs 1.383 (DH) over 540 points ⇒ ghost-blind; it only constrains ζ(w) ≠ 0 for Re w > 1 (already known).

concepts.name: Metaplectic / Kubota cocycle
concepts.plain: A 2-valued cocycle on SL₂ behind half-integer weight; structure without sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §4: Kubota cocycle is a phase (Ax3); Hilbert product formula 300/300, quadratic reciprocity; θ weight ½ is metaplectic (a fourth root, TAA Lemma 141 §7) — mod 2 data, ghost-blind.

concepts.name: The prime 2 as the wild place
concepts.plain: The only even prime is 2 (not √2). At 2 the Gauss halves break: (p − 1)/2 is not an integer, every model y² = f(x) has bad reduction, and the Hilbert symbol / metaplectic cocycle is wild. √2 enters through (2/p), which depends on p mod 8.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Supplementary law: (2/p) = +1 ⇔ p ≡ ±1 mod 8; √2 ∈ ℚ(ζ₈), so (2/p) is the character χ₈ (the √2 family). At p = 2, (p − 1)/2 is not an integer and every Weierstrass model y² = f(x) is bad at 2; the Hilbert symbol and the metaplectic (Kubota) cocycle are wild at 2. All of this is phase data, hence ghost-blind.
pitfalls: The even prime is 2, not √2; √2 appears only through the character (2/p) = χ₈(p).

rels.note: wild at 2: Hilbert symbol / Kubota cocycle

concepts.name: Scattering unitarity |φ| = 1
concepts.plain: The cusp scattering coefficient has modulus one on the critical line — true with or without RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |φ(½ + it)| = 1 follows from the functional equation; it is Ax3 (adjoint) only and ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Not Rosati: only the ππ† = q half.

concepts.name: Eisenstein constant term & scattering φ(s)
concepts.plain: The Eisenstein series’ constant term has two pieces linked by φ(s); on Re s = ½ |φ| = 1 for any zeros — a phase statement.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s); |φ(½+it)| = 1 unconditionally (unitarity of scattering). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: |φ| = 1 is only Ax3.

concepts.name: Gauss half: quadratic character, (p ± 1)/2 and the (p + 1)/4 square-root formula
concepts.plain: Every odd prime p splits the nonzero residues into (p − 1)/2 squares and (p − 1)/2 non-squares; the quadratic character (x/p) records which. For an elliptic curve y² = f(x), a_p is minus the sum of these characters, and its value mod p is a Gauss-half power.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: a_p = −Σ_x (f(x)/p) for y² = f(x); Hasse: a_p ≡ coefficient of x^{p−1} in f^{(p−1)/2} mod p. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, (p + 1)/4 is an integer and √a = a^{(p+1)/4} mod p (691 → 173). y² = x³ − x: a_p = −2, 6, 2 for p = 5, 13, 17; a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, so N₆₉₁ = 692. The Gauss halves see only the coherent H¹(E, 𝒪), i.e. a_p mod p; the bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p needs positivity (Castelnuovo/Hodge index).
pitfalls: a_p mod p is phase-type information; it does not give the size bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
The ½ of (p ± 1)/2 is a counting half; relating it to the half-density ½ is an analogy.

rels.note: the ½ in (p ± 1)/2 vs the unitary |x|^{½} twist; analogy
mod-p data cannot give the size bound; that needs Castelnuovo–Severi

concepts.name: Half-density normalization |x|^{½}
concepts.plain: Multiplying by |x|^{½} makes scaling unitary on L²; this is why the critical line is at ½.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145 Thm twist: |x|^½ = (dx/d*x)^½ is unitary L²(dx) → L²(d*x); U_λ unitary with generator −(x∂_x + ½); Mellin is unitary only on Re s = ½ (Plancherel 0.35355339 both sides; at Re 0.4 a weighted norm 0.53173). Cusp gauge y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4).
pitfalls: There are two ½’s (TAA Lemma 145 corrections): the unitary twist and the critical line.

concepts.name: Hilbert reciprocity at 2: the odd halves become sign bits
concepts.plain: At odd primes the halves (p − 1)/2 count squares; at 2 the corresponding quantities ε(u) = (u − 1)/2 and ω(u) = (u² − 1)/8 are sign bits. Hilbert reciprocity says the sign at 2 is fixed by the odd places and ∞. This is phase information, not positivity.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: (−1/p) = (−1)^{ε(p)}, (2/p) = (−1)^{ω(p)}. 2-adic Hilbert symbol: for a = 2^α u, b = 2^β v with u, v odd units, (a,b)₂ = (−1)^{ε(u)ε(v) + αω(v) + βω(u)} (Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III, Thm 1). Product formula ∏ᵥ (a,b)ᵥ = 1 over all places including ∞ ⇒ the 2-adic sign is determined by the odd places and ∞; it is a restatement of quadratic reciprocity with both supplementary laws. ℚ₂^×/squares has order 8; ℤ₂^×/squares = {±1, ±5} has order 4: two sign bits, ε (sign of −1) and ω (the √2 / χ₈ bit). Checked: product formula holds for 3000 random pairs |a|, |b| ≤ 5000; ε, ω for u = 1, 3, 5, 7: (0,0), (1,1), (0,1), (1,0). Phase data (Ax3), ghost-blind: Davenport–Heilbronn shares the same reciprocity.
concepts.uncertain: to verify: Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III Thm 1 not opened here; formula re-checked numerically via the product formula only.
pitfalls: The sign at 2 is a reciprocity sign (phase), not the positivity sign of RH; reading it as the half-density counterpart is an analogy.
Equivalent to quadratic reciprocity, not to RH.

rels.note: odd halves (p ± 1)/2 ↔ sign bits ε, ω at 2
Hilbert symbol = the cocycle behind the metaplectic cover

concepts.name: Counts vs quadratic positivity
concepts.plain: Point counts being positive does not force RH; only quadratic forms can.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 109: 2935 count-positive ghosts (g = 2, q = 11).

concepts.name: w₂ / Čech class (TAA Lemma 138)
concepts.plain: Obstruction class to a spin structure, tested as a candidate arithmetic object (TAA Lemma 138).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 138: the Čech 2-class (polarization, c₁) supplies the pairing, † and Ax3 (π*L ≅ L^q) for free; spin supplies mod-2 refinements only; the sign is always ampleness. TAA Lemma 141 §7: w₂ = c₁ mod 2; half-densities are canonical (no w₂); w₂ governs half-forms (K^{1/2} = ω weight 1).
pitfalls: w₂ is not for densities (TAA Lemma 141 list).

concepts.name: Weight ladder (modular weights)
concepts.plain: Modular forms come in weights; at each rung the Eisenstein series E_k is the reference. A “stratification” of modular structures is this ladder.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 corrections: stratification = weight ladder, with E_k the reference per rung; cusp positivity on each rung is ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 139 weight-1 search: weight-1 modular = motivic weight 0 (η(z)η(23z), |α| = 1); motivic weight 1 = weight-2 cusp forms (11a, Rosati PD); ζ appears only in Eisenstein lines (ζ_K weight 1, ζ(s)ζ(s−1) weight 2), not in L².

rels.note: cusp positivity per rung is ghost-blind

concepts.name: Yoshida window positivity
concepts.plain: For test functions supported in a small enough window, Weil positivity holds unconditionally.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Yoshida: W ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ small window; TAA Lemma 10 window ≤ log 3. Below ghost onsets, so ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Unconditional windows never reach ghost onset.

concepts.name: Cup product / Poincaré duality pairing
concepts.plain: The pairing of cohomology classes; it gives the duality partner of a zero, ghosts included.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Duality partner via cup product (TAA Lemma 93); positivity needs conjugate + Hodge structure (HR).

concepts.name: Theta inversion θ(1/t) = √t θ(t)
concepts.plain: Poisson summation gives the functional equation; phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(1/x) = √x θ(x) gives Riemann’s FE and the boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) of 1/(s(s−1)) (TAA Lemma 36 §6). TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion for x² + 5y² to 3e−30; Weil representation unitary, (ST)³ = Gauss sum · I; unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 145: θ FE error 6.3e−26; TAA Lemma 146: θ S-error ≤ 2.5e−16, Fresnel = half-density × Weil index.

concepts.name: Bost–Connes KMS states
concepts.plain: A quantum statistical system whose partition function is ζ(β); its positive KMS states and phase transition at β = 1 see ζ only at real β > 1, never the zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: BC95 (Thm 5; CM08 3.32): Q-structure, Gal(Q^cycl/Q) symmetry, positive KMS states, ζ(β) real for β > 1; no trace equal to the Weil distribution found (TAA Lemma 30). TAA Lemma 38: strongest rigorous bridge; BC time is dual to rapidity, (β,t) = (Re s, −Im s); BC ordered phase ⇔ ω > ½. TAA Lemma 39: BC = tensor product over primes twisted by Galois. TAA Lemma 54/TAA Lemma 118: KMS/passivity uses ζ at real β > 1 ⇒ ghost-blind.
pitfalls: BC95 Thm 5(a) states β < 1 (β ≤ 1 from CM08 3.32) (TAA Lemma 38 flag).

concepts.name: Spin structure & theta characteristic
concepts.plain: Theta characteristics = spin structures = square roots of the canonical bundle; they refine the Weil pairing mod 2 and are shared by fakes and true curves alike.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 136: theta chars = spin structures = quadratic refinements of the Weil pairing; Arf counts 3/1, 10/6, 36/28, 136/120, 528/496 (g ≤ 5); K^{1/2} = fixed points of D ↦ K − D = self-dual centre s = ½ [R]. TAA Lemma 138 R3 (exhaustive g ≤ 2): #Frobenius-fixed theta chars = #J[2](F_q); fakes share mod-2 data with true curves ⇒ ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 141 §7: w₂ governs half-forms (K^{1/2}), not half-densities.
pitfalls: "Spec ℤ not spin": the real place obstructs a half twist — analogy only (TAA Lemma 50 Rem 7.3).

concepts.name: "Cocycles give structure, not sign"
concepts.plain: Any cocycle/class (metaplectic, w₂, defect) fixes structure but cannot decide a positivity sign.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 138/TAA Lemma 144/TAA Lemma 146 summary principle.

concepts.name: Buoyancy / Archimedes principle
concepts.plain: Weight is measured relative to the fluid displaced; Castelnuovo–Severi and the pole subtraction can be read the same way.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: C–S as D² = 2ab + D′² — Archimedes relative to U; the sign is an input (fluids), proved (curves), ⇔ RH (ζ). Buoyancy sign as input: TAA Lemma 146 corrections.
pitfalls: Analogy, not a mechanism.

concepts.name: Heaviside RLGC line
concepts.plain: Transmission line with resistance, inductance, conductance, capacitance; used as a model for β.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25: {R/L, G/C} = {β, 1 − β} in τ, orientation conventional (Prop 3.3); TAA Lemma 143 R/2L ↔ β/2; TAA Lemma 144 unordered {(1−β)/2, β/2} in u.
pitfalls: The R/L, G/C ordering is a convention and differs between TAA Lemmas 25, 143 and 144.

concepts.name: Mass-density positivity
concepts.plain: Single positive quantity (like mass) as model for Rosati.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: N² = −(g/ρ)ρ′ (buoyancy frequency); the sign of the density gradient is an input for fluids, proved for curves, ⇔ RH for ζ.

concepts.name: Distortionless line R/L = G/C
concepts.plain: Line that transmits without distortion; corresponds to β = ½.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25/TAA Lemma 143: distortionless ⇔ β = ½.

concepts.name: Anomalous dispersion
concepts.plain: Phase behavior near a line; ghost-blind.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36: anomalous dispersion = analogy — gain lines are where absorption and phase disagree; THM 4.3 absorption–phase sum rule ∫₀ᵀ Re ξ′/ξ(σ₀+it)dt = π[N(T) − 2N(σ₀,T)] + …, deficit 2πN(σ₀,T) ≥ 0 (leads to zero density, not a proof). TAA Lemma 78: causality versus linewidth, Kramers–Kronig for the modular scattering matrix. TAA Lemma 146: dRe χ/dω at centre −6 (absorber) vs +6 (gain).

concepts.name: Lamb cutoff
concepts.plain: In a stratified fluid, waves below the Lamb cutoff frequency c/2H cannot propagate; on the modular surface the cusp’s −¼ is exactly this cutoff with scale height H = 1.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: with dy/y² = e^{−r}dr, the cusp −¼ equals the Lamb cutoff c/2H with H = 1 (exact operator identity); TAA Lemma 141 §6: the cusp is a Webster horn A = e^{−r}, Liouville factor e^{r/2}, and +¼ cancels the horn cutoff. Same −¼ as y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4) (TAA Lemma 145).
pitfalls: Lamb’s original source not opened (TAA Lemma 146 refs); the identity is checked as an operator identity.

concepts.name: Two different χ’s: Euler characteristic vs class-group character
concepts.plain: The χ of the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch on the square is an Euler characteristic of a divisor; the χ¹¹ / ω⁻¹¹ of the 691 story is a Galois character labelling an eigenspace. Different objects; any link is an analogy.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (TAA Lemma 145/TAA Lemma 147, a number for each divisor) vs Teichmüller / cyclotomic character ω, χ_cyc (TAA Lemma 66, labels of eigenspaces of Cl(ℚ(μ₆₉₁)) and of ρ_Δ mod 691). Shared shape only: Mazur–Wiles equates an algebraic size with an L-value, as RR equates χ with degree + constant. Neither sees the sign of D² (Iwasawa: sizes; CC RR: linear χ).
concepts.uncertain: The analogy itself is interpretive; no TAA lemma relates the two.
pitfalls: Do not identify them: notation clash only.
Iwasawa measures sizes, never the sign of D².

concepts.name: Standard conjectures (Hodge type)
concepts.plain: The higher-dimensional version of Hodge index in characteristic p; known for surfaces, open in general.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Hodge standard conjecture: known in char 0 and for surfaces, abelian fourfolds (Ancona 2021), K3² (IIK 2022); open in general char p, dim ≥ 3. Common root of Hodge, BSD and RH over F_q; analogy over ℚ (TAA Lemma 88).
pitfalls: TAA Lemma 89, correction 4: unrefereed preprint claim (CM Hodge ⇒ standard conjecture) flagged, not applied.
